key_insight: Clipped decentralized SGD can achieve order-optimal convergence under heavy-tailed gradient noise while preserving linear speed-up across agents, unlike some normalized decentralized methods.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical, scalable optimization baseline for distributed machine learning systems operating in noisy, non-IID, or heavy-tailed regimes.
method: Apply gradient clipping to local stochastic gradients before decentralized averaging.
Analyze non-convex smooth objectives under bounded p-th moment noise with p in (1,2].
Derive sharp consensus-gap bounds showing network effects enter only as higher-order terms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports both high-probability and expectation guarantees, plus numerical experiments that validate the theory.
watch_item: Clipping threshold choice may be sensitive in practice and overly aggressive clipping can bias updates if not tuned carefully.
paper_title: Decentralized SGD under Heavy-Tailed Noise: Optimal Convergence Rates and the Role of Gradient Clipping
